Google Study Shows 90% of Tech Jobs Will Require AI Skills

By Sarah Chen, CNN Tech | Updated September 23, 2025

A groundbreaking study released by Google on Monday reveals that an estimated 90 percent of technology jobs will require some level of artificial intelligence expertise within the next five years, signaling a massive shift in the skills landscape for the tech industry.

The study, conducted by Google's AI research division in partnership with Stanford University and MIT, surveyed over 10,000 tech companies across 45 countries and analyzed more than 2 million job postings from the past three years.

"We're seeing a fundamental transformation in what it means to work in technology," said Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet, Google's parent company. "AI is no longer a specialized field — it's becoming as essential as knowing how to use a computer."

Key findings from the study include:

  • Machine learning engineering roles have grown 340% since 2022
  • Traditional software engineering positions increasingly list AI/ML as a required skill
  • Companies with AI-integrated workflows report 45% higher productivity
  • The demand for AI skills extends beyond engineering to product management, design, and marketing roles

The report also highlights a significant skills gap. According to the data, only 25% of current tech workers have received formal AI training, despite the growing demand. This gap is particularly pronounced in mid-career professionals who completed their education before the recent AI boom.

Dr. Andrew Ng, a prominent AI researcher and founder of DeepLearning.AI, called the findings "consistent with what we've been observing in the industry."

"The question is no longer whether AI will transform tech jobs — it's how quickly organizations can adapt their workforce," Ng said in a statement.

The study recommends that companies invest in reskilling programs and that educational institutions update their curricula to include AI fundamentals across all technology disciplines.

Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta have already announced expanded AI training programs for their employees. Google itself has committed $500 million to AI education initiatives over the next three years.

Industry analysts at Goldman Sachs estimate that the AI skills transition could affect approximately 30 million tech workers globally by 2030.
